subject: Computer Networking
title: JMAP — The Modern Protocol
description: A micro-lesson that makes JMAP — The Modern Protocol usable.

hook.text: IMAP is from 1986. JMAP is its modern replacement — JSON-based, efficient, and developer-friendly.

buildup.text: JMAP uses HTTP and JSON. No custom binary protocol. Web developers feel right at home.

discovery.text: JMAP syncs only changes. Instead of re-downloading folders, it sends a tiny delta. Way less bandwidth.

twist.text: JMAP handles mail, calendars, and contacts in one protocol. IMAP needed separate standards for each.

climax.text: Fastmail built JMAP and contributed it as an IETF standard. Adoption is growing but still early.

punchline.text: JMAP modernizes email sync. JSON over HTTP, finally.

quiz.question: What data format does JMAP use?

details.summary: JSON Meta Application Protocol is a modern email protocol designed to replace IMAP. JMAP uses efficient JSON over HTTP, supports push notifications, and handles email, contacts, and calendars. It eliminates many of IMAP's problems with synchronization, bandwidth, and mobile efficiency.
details.whyItMatters: JMAP is the future of email access protocols. It solves fundamental problems with IMAP that have frustrated developers and consumed battery life on mobile devices for decades.
takeaways: JMAP uses efficient JSON over HTTP, replacing IMAP's text protocol
It supports push notifications without persistent connections
JMAP handles email, contacts, and calendars in one protocol

faq.question: What problems does JMAP solve that IMAP cannot?
faq.answer: IMAP requires a persistent connection and generates excessive round trips for synchronization. JMAP batches operations efficiently over stateless HTTP. It supports native push notifications without holding connections open. It handles partial sync efficiently, saving mobile battery.

faq.question: Is JMAP widely supported?
faq.answer: Adoption is growing but still limited. Fastmail developed and champions JMAP. It is standardized as RFC 8620. Most major email clients have not yet added JMAP support because IMAP inertia is strong. Adoption will accelerate as mobile efficiency becomes more important.
